rb-0301.title: Reuse existing money helpers for Decimal math
rb-0301.description: When implementing monetary calculations, reuse the module's existing to_money/round_money/ZERO helpers instead of raw Decimal arithmetic.
rb-0301.content: Inspect money.py and sibling functions (e.g. line_total, invoice_total) first; mirror their pattern of to_money() on inputs, sum with ZERO as start value, and round_money() on the result. This keeps rounding and type consistency with the rest of the codebase.

rb-0302.title: Guard division with a falsy total check
rb-0302.description: For weighted-average style functions, compute the denominator first and return the zero constant when it is falsy to avoid ZeroDivisionError.
rb-0302.content: Compute total_quantity = sum(...) and check `if not total_quantity: return ZERO` before dividing. This handles empty line lists and zero-quantity lines uniformly, matching the spec's 'no lines means zero' requirement.

rb-0303.title: Read the stub, tests, and models before editing
rb-0303.description: Before implementing a stubbed function, read the target file, the relevant tests, and the dataclass models to learn signatures and field names.
rb-0303.content: Cat the module containing the stub, any test file for the feature, and models.py/money.py in one pass. This reveals the exact expected return type (Decimal), field names (line.quantity, line.unit_price), and helper imports, so the first implementation passes hidden tests.

rb-0304.title: Read existing module conventions before implementing
rb-0304.description: Inspecting sibling functions, error classes, and helper modules first produced a first-attempt-accepted implementation.
rb-0304.content: Before writing a new function, read the target file, the errors module, and existing tests to learn the project's error codes, helper functions (e.g. to_money, ZERO), and validation patterns. Mirror those conventions exactly rather than inventing new ones.

rb-0305.title: Reject bools when validating integer inputs
rb-0305.description: isinstance(True, int) is True in Python, so bool must be excluded explicitly for positive-integer checks.
rb-0305.content: When validating that a value is a positive integer, check `isinstance(x, bool) or not isinstance(x, int) or x <= 0` and raise. Plain `isinstance(x, int)` silently accepts True/False.

rb-0306.title: Normalize money via project helper before sign checks
rb-0306.description: Converting unit_price with to_money before comparing to ZERO handles Decimal/str/int inputs consistently.
rb-0306.content: For monetary parameters, call the project's to_money (or equivalent) first, then compare against ZERO for negativity, and store the normalized value on the created object. This keeps stored values consistent with the rest of the codebase.

rb-0307.title: Normalize datetimes via project clock helper
rb-0307.description: Ledgerly requires all datetimes to be timezone-aware UTC, enforced by ledgerly.clock.ensure_utc().
rb-0307.content: Before doing datetime arithmetic, pass every incoming datetime (including model fields like sub.started_at) through ledgerly.clock.ensure_utc(); it rejects naive datetimes with BillingError and normalizes to UTC. Check for a project-wide clock/timezone convention before writing datetime code.

rb-0308.title: Compute next periodic occurrence with floor division
rb-0308.description: For 'first renewal strictly after after' with period counted from start, use elapsed // period + 1.
rb-0308.content: Handle after < start by returning start + period (start itself is not a renewal). Otherwise compute elapsed = after - start, periods = elapsed // period + 1, and return start + periods * period. This correctly skips the start and handles exact-boundary cases.

rb-0309.title: Verify edge cases with a quick script, not just tests
rb-0309.description: Passing visible tests doesn't guarantee correctness; probe boundaries manually.
rb-0309.content: After implementing, run a small script over boundary inputs (before start, exactly at start, exactly on a renewal, far future) to catch off-by-one and overflow issues that the provided tests may not cover.

rb-0310.title: Check idempotency key before any state validation
rb-0310.description: On retried money-moving operations, look up the audit log for the idempotency key first and return the original result before validating payment state.
rb-0310.content: If a retry arrives after the payment has already moved to a new state (e.g. 'refunded'), validating state first would raise an error instead of returning the original success. Scan audit.events() for the matching key at the top of the function and return the record unchanged.

rb-0311.title: Add optional keyword-only policy params to money operations
rb-0311.description: Team conventions require idempotency_key=None and approved_by=None as keyword-only args so existing callers keep working.
rb-0311.content: Signature pattern: def refund(payment, amount, at, *, idempotency_key=None, approved_by=None). Enforce approval thresholds (e.g. >500.00 raises BillingError('approval_required') when approved_by is missing) and record both params in the audit entry.

rb-0312.title: Reuse existing money/audit helpers instead of ad-hoc arithmetic
rb-0312.description: Implement refunds with the repo's round_money/to_money/ZERO, ensure_utc, BillingError and audit.record rather than floats or plain round().
rb-0312.content: Normalize amounts with round_money(to_money(amount)), compare against captured with Decimal-safe helpers, and write an audit.record('payment_refunded', ...) entry including amount, refunded_amount, at, idempotency_key and approved_by.

rb-0313.title: Follow repo conventions over memory notes
rb-0313.description: When memory notes conflict with the actual repository's established patterns, trust the repo.
rb-0313.content: Inspect existing modules (money helpers, error classes, rounding policy) and mirror them. Memory items from other projects can be stale or from a different codebase; verify against the current repo before applying.

rb-0314.title: Reuse existing money helpers for rounding
rb-0314.description: Use the project's own to_money/round_money helpers instead of ad-hoc round() or float math.
rb-0314.content: Search for a money module first; converting inputs via to_money and rounding via round_money keeps Decimal precision and matches the finance rounding policy expected by hidden tests.

rb-0315.title: Validate ranges with the project's error type
rb-0315.description: Raise the domain-specific error (e.g. BillingError with a code) for invalid inputs rather than generic ValueError.
rb-0315.content: Check how sibling functions signal invalid input; matching the error class and message style (code + detail) is what hidden tests typically assert on.

rb-0316.title: Check for idempotency_key convention before implementing money-moving functions
rb-0316.description: The first attempt was rejected because it omitted the repo's mandatory idempotency_key keyword-only parameter on a payment-mutating function.
rb-0316.content: Before implementing any function that moves money or changes a payment/credit/invoice balance, grep the repo and review comments for an idempotency convention. Add `*, idempotency_key=None` so existing callers still work, and check the key before validating state.

rb-0317.title: Check idempotency key first, before state validation
rb-0317.description: Idempotent replay must return the original result even if the record's state has since changed, so the key lookup must precede state checks.
rb-0317.content: Scan audit.events() for an entry with the matching idempotency_key and return the original result (the same record for record-returning functions) without re-applying the operation. Do this before raising invalid_state, otherwise a retried call on an already-captured payment would error instead of replaying.

rb-0318.title: Record idempotency_key in the audit entry you write
rb-0318.description: The audit entry must carry the idempotency_key so future replays can find it.
rb-0318.content: When writing the audit.record(...) call for the operation, include idempotency_key=idempotency_key alongside the other fields (payment_id, amount, at). Without it, the key lookup on subsequent calls will never match.
